title: Canada Fires Back in Trade War Against Trump With Up to 50% Tariffs
partialText: Canada said the higher levies, on items from aluminum foil to dishwashers to fish, would help protect workers, producers and manufacturers harmed by new Trump tariffs.

title: Trump’s Canada Tariffs Rely on Untested Law
partialText: The president has invoked a long dormant section of law to hit one of America’s closest allies, a move that has troubled courts in the past.

title: How U.S.-Canada Tariff Negotiations Turned Into an All-Out Trade War
partialText: Detailed accounts of the final hours of the negotiations show that, while the United States offered Canada what it said was the best deal of any country, what Canada had to give up in exchange was seen as unthinkable.

title: At Least 1 in 4 NFL Players Gets CTE, Major New Study Finds
partialText: The actual prevalence, researchers said, may be much higher.

title: Many N.F.L. Players Get Brain Disease. Why Hasn’t OSHA Intervened?

title: Your Child Plays Football. How Can You Minimize Risk of C.T.E.?
partialText: Researchers say it’s all about reducing the total number of blows to the head.

title: China Pushes Back After Trump Tightens the Screws on Iran

title: Iran May Have Little to Lose as U.S. Tries to Squeeze Its Economy
partialText: Experts warn that a campaign aimed at avoiding military escalation could instead provoke it, as Iranian leaders vow retaliation across the oil-rich Gulf.

title: Supreme Court Allows Trump to Pursue Mail Voting Limits, for Now
partialText: The administration asked the court to clear the way for President Trump’s order that creates “state citizenship lists” and directs the Postal Service to decide who gets a mail-in ballot.

title: Trump Wants to Restrict Mail-In Voting. See Which States Rely on It The Most.
partialText: Nearly 30 percent of voters nationwide use mail ballots. President Trump is seeking greater federal control of mail voting.

title: Is the Supreme Court’s Shadow Docket Changing?
partialText: The Supreme Court’s emergency docket has shrunk in recent months, and the way justices issue opinions on these cases has also changed. Our reporter Ann Marimow looks at what these shifts tell us about the justices, and what it could mean for the court.

title: In Pennsylvania, 2 Measles Deaths Are Reported
partialText: The deaths, which one doctor called “extremely rare in the modern era,” are the first in the United States in 2026.

title: Trump Lawyers Warn That Kennedy Center Might Need Demolition if Not Fixed
partialText: In a court filing about honoring President Trump on the facade, the administration said that without a proper renovation the building might need to be “taken down.”

title: John Fetterman’s Popularity With Republicans Surges, Poll Finds
partialText: Pennsylvania Republicans now view John Fetterman, the state’s Democratic senator, more favorably than its sitting G.O.P. senator, a New York Times/Philadelphia Inquirer/Siena poll found.

title: Poll Shows Josh Shapiro Leading Pennsylvania Governor’s Race
partialText: A New York Times/Philadelphia Inquirer/Siena poll found Gov. Josh Shapiro leading Stacy Garrity and having support in the state for a possible presidential bid.

title: ‘They Opened the Door and Pulled Us Out’: How ICE Descended on a Town
partialText: One summer morning, immigration agents swooped in and detained 18 immigrants at a store in Lakewood, N.J., plunging the town into fear.

title: Christian Convert Who Fled Iran and Was Deported By Trump Finds New Home
partialText: Artemis Ghasemzadeh, who had escaped religious persecution, was deported to Panama under Trump’s immigration crackdown. Now, Canada has given her asylum.

title: Lawmakers Push Hochul to Block ICE From Taking Over Upstate Warehouse
partialText: As a state law preventing the police from working with federal immigration officials goes into effect, a potential plan to use a warehouse as a detention center has drawn outrage.

title: Democratic Senators Ask Homeland Security for Details About Idled Planes
partialText: The request follows a New York Times story, which revealed that Homeland Security had spent $464 million on used jets that rarely fly.

title: Why Irregular’s A.I. Tests for Meta, Anthropic and OpenAI Went Off the Rails
partialText: Irregular, an Israeli start-up, worked with OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta to assess the security of their A.I. models. It made a mistake. Then the tests went off the rails.

title: A Chinese A.I. Lab May Test the World’s Cybersecurity With a Model
partialText: In July, an unreleased OpenAI model went rogue and demonstrated remarkable hacking abilities. This week, a lab called Z.ai will release a similarly powerful system to everyone.

title: This A.I. Start-Up Aims to Reverse the Backlash Against Data Centers
partialText: Emerald AI, now valued at $1.05 billion, uses software to keep power demand at the computing facilities from getting out of control.

title: 3 Charts That Explain El Niño

title: We Know the Risks of A.I. We Need to Act.

title: Religious References in Lindsay Clancy Trial Anger Judge and Defense
partialText: The religious reference by a prosecution witness on Monday incensed the presiding judge, who sternly instructed jurors to disregard it. Lindsay Clancy’s lawyer asked for a mistrial.
